question: Which statement best describes The discriminant tag?
options: Each member of the union has a shared property whose type is a unique string (or numeric) literal — the discriminant. Because the tags are distinct literals, TypeScript can tell members apart just by reading that one field, no other check needed.

A switch over the discriminant with one case per variant handles every possibility. Adding a default that asserts never turns 'I forgot a case' into a compile error, so the switch is provably exhaustive.

When all variants are handled, the value's type in the default branch is never. Passing it to assertNever(x: never) compiles only while exhaustive; introduce a new variant and the call errors, pointing at the missing case.

Checking the tag (if (s.kind === 'a') or a switch case) narrows the value to the single matching variant. Inside that branch you can access that variant's unique fields safely — the others are eliminated from the type.
